command: benchmark/hg002/run_wholegenome.sh (per-chrom bcftools consensus + scan_variant_axis.py + panisoguard adjudicate variant axis); totals over chr1-22
data_provenance: real GIAB HG002/NA24385 v4.2.1 benchmark variants (biallelic SNVs), whole-genome chr1-22, GRCh38 + GENCODE v49. Per chromosome: bcftools SNV-consensus haplotype, then scan every annotation intron's donor/acceptor dinucleotide for reference bias (non-canonical on the linear reference, canonical on the HG002 haplotype = CREATED), and adjudicate the variant axis (--haplotype-provenance wgs for the rescue, unknown for the firewall). Annotation+variant scan; no RNA-seq/caller runs. No private data.
notes: Whole-genome yield of the variant reference-bias rescue (extends the chr22 N=1 result). Reference bias at splice junctions is rare but not zero: 33 reference-bias junctions across 597,781 introns (~1 in 18,000). The axis rescued all 33 (33/33) with 0 false rescues; the circularity firewall holds all 33 under circular-risk provenance. The rescue is a check with a low base rate, not a discovery method; its yield rises for samples from non-reference individuals or personalized-genome contexts. DISRUPTED (236, canonical->non-canonical) is computed but not consumed by the engine, so it is never rescued.
